::: {.route-question}
Question for today: a worn die lip makes the coating drift slowly heavier. Which chart notices first?
:::

## Rational subgroups {#subgroups}

::: {.two}
::: {}
Each hour, five coupons are punched across the web at the same moment: one **subgroup**.

Variation **within** a subgroup is short-term, common-cause noise. Variation **between** subgroups adds anything that changes over time.

Control limits are built from within-subgroup variation, so a shift between hours stands out.
:::
::: {}
::: {.route-question}
A poor choice: five coupons taken over five hours as one subgroup. Hour-to-hour drift then inflates the ranges, widens the limits and hides the drift it should reveal.
:::
:::
:::

## X-bar and R charts for mass loading {#xbar-r}

::: {.two}
::: {}
25 subgroups of 5 coupons: grand mean x̿ = **20.05**, mean range R̄ = **0.40** mg/cm².

```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Chart</th><th>Limits</th><th class="num">mg/cm²</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>X-bar</td><td>x̿ ± A<sub>2</sub>R̄ = 20.05 ± 0.577 × 0.40</td><td class="num hit">19.82 to 20.28</td></tr>
    <tr><td>R</td><td>D<sub>3</sub>R̄ to D<sub>4</sub>R̄ = 0 to 2.114 × 0.40</td><td class="num">0 to 0.85</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Process σ</td><td>R̄ / d<sub>2</sub> = 0.40 / 2.326</td><td class="num">0.172</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```
:::
::: {}
**Read the R chart first.** If within-subgroup spread is not stable, the X-bar limits, which use R̄, mean nothing.

**Control limits are not specification limits.** Limits describe what the process does (19.82 to 20.28 for subgroup means); the specification describes what the customer needs (19.4 to 20.6 for single coupons).

[Constants for subgroups of 5: A~2~ = 0.577, D~3~ = 0, D~4~ = 2.114, d~2~ = 2.326.]{.hint}
:::
:::

## Individuals data and run rules {#imr-rules}

::: {.two}
::: {}
**I-MR chart.** When one reading arrives at a time (one viscosity test per slurry batch), chart the individual values, with σ estimated from the average moving range: σ = MR̄ / 1.128.

**Western Electric run rules.** Signal if:

1. One point beyond 3σ.
2. Two of three successive points beyond 2σ on the same side.
3. Four of five beyond 1σ on the same side.
4. Eight in a row on one side of the center line.
:::
::: {}
::: {.route-question}
Each rule added catches smaller shifts sooner, but also raises false alarms. With all four rules, an in-control process gives a false alarm about every 92 subgroups instead of every 370.
:::
:::
:::

## Why Shewhart charts miss small shifts {#arl}

```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Average run length, subgroups</th><th class="num">In control</th><th class="num">Shift 0.5 σ<sub>x̄</sub></th><th class="num">Shift 1.0 σ<sub>x̄</sub></th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>X-bar chart, 3σ limits</td><td class="num">370</td><td class="num">155</td><td class="num">44</td></tr>
    <tr><td>CUSUM, k = 0.5, h = 4.77</td><td class="num">370</td><td class="num">35</td><td class="num">10</td></tr>
    <tr><td>EWMA, λ = 0.1, L = 2.7</td><td class="num">370</td><td class="num hit">25</td><td class="num">7.5</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

::: {.bridge}
All three charts raise a false alarm about once every 370 subgroups. For a shift of half a standard error, 0.04 mg/cm², the X-bar chart needs about 155 hours, almost a week of production, to notice; EWMA needs about 25.
:::

[Run lengths from simulation, as checked for this course. σ~x̄~ = 0.172 / √5 = 0.077 mg/cm².]{.note-line}

## Charts with memory {#ewma-cusum}

::: {.two}
::: {}
**EWMA** (exponentially weighted moving average)

z~t~ = λ x̄~t~ + (1 − λ) z~t−1~, starting at z~0~ = 20.05

With λ = 0.1, each new subgroup gets 10% weight and older subgroups fade. Limits narrow to 20.05 ± 0.048 mg/cm².
:::
::: {}
**CUSUM** (cumulative sum)

C~t~ = max(0, C~t−1~ + (x̄~t~ − 20.05)/σ~x̄~ − k)

Small deviations in one direction accumulate; the sum signals when it exceeds h. A matching lower CUSUM catches drifts downward.
:::
:::

[Both charts trade a slower response to one large jump for a much faster response to small sustained shifts. Many lines run a Shewhart chart and an EWMA side by side.]{.note-line}

## Drift detectives {#drift-explorer data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="widget" id="ddx">
  <div class="w-controls"><button type="button" class="w-btn" id="ddx-next">Next subgroup</button> <button type="button" class="w-choice" id="ddx-all">Show all 30</button> <button type="button" class="w-choice" id="ddx-rst">Restart</button> <span id="ddx-n" style="margin-left:1em"></span></div>
  <svg id="ddx-svg" viewBox="0 0 1160 300" role="img" aria-label="X-bar chart and EWMA chart for coating subgroups revealed so far"></svg>
  <div class="w-readout" id="ddx-out" aria-live="polite"></div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('ddx'); if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  const xs = [20.179,20.043,19.994,20.128,20.014,19.973,20.132,20.115,20.123,20.115,20.100,20.081,19.962,20.114,20.128,20.217,20.076,20.129,20.033,20.131,20.054,20.207,20.169,20.013,20.164,20.139,20.153,20.112,20.080,20.074];
  const MU = 20.05, SX = 0.172 / Math.sqrt(5), LAM = 0.1, LL = 2.7, N = xs.length;
  const ew = [], lim = []; let z = MU;
  xs.forEach((x, i) => { z = LAM * x + (1 - LAM) * z; ew.push(z); lim.push(LL * SX * Math.sqrt(LAM / (2 - LAM) * (1 - (1 - LAM) ** (2 * (i + 1))))); });
  const sigX = xs.findIndex((x) => Math.abs(x - MU) > 3 * SX), sigE = ew.findIndex((v, i) => Math.abs(v - MU) > lim[i]);
  let shown = 0;
  function panel(y0, h, lo, hi, vals, center, ucl, lcl, sig, col, label) {
    const L = 70, R = 20, X = (i) => L + i / (N - 1) * (1160 - L - R), Y = (v) => y0 + (1 - (v - lo) / (hi - lo)) * h;
    let g = `<text x="${L}" y="${y0 - 6}" font-size="15" font-weight="700" fill="#1C242B">${label}</text>`;
    g += `<line x1="${L}" x2="${1160 - R}" y1="${Y(center)}" y2="${Y(center)}" stroke="#B9C1C6"/>`;
    let pu = '', pl = ''; for (let i = 0; i < N; i++) { pu += (i ? 'L' : 'M') + X(i).toFixed(1) + ',' + Y(ucl(i)).toFixed(1); pl += (i ? 'L' : 'M') + X(i).toFixed(1) + ',' + Y(lcl(i)).toFixed(1); }
    g += `<path d="${pu}" fill="none" stroke="#BE654C" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><path d="${pl}" fill="none" stroke="#BE654C" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>`;
    g += `<text x="${L - 8}" y="${Y(hi) + 12}" text-anchor="end" font-size="13" fill="#333F4A">${hi.toFixed(2)}</text><text x="${L - 8}" y="${Y(lo)}" text-anchor="end" font-size="13" fill="#333F4A">${lo.toFixed(2)}</text>`;
    let p = ''; for (let i = 0; i < shown; i++) p += (i ? 'L' : 'M') + X(i).toFixed(1) + ',' + Y(vals[i]).toFixed(1);
    g += `<path d="${p}" fill="none" stroke="${col}" stroke-width="2"/>`;
    for (let i = 0; i < shown; i++) g += `<circle cx="${X(i)}" cy="${Y(vals[i])}" r="${i === sig ? 7 : 4}" fill="${i >= sig && sig >= 0 && Math.abs(vals[i] - center) > Math.abs(ucl(i) - center) ? '#BE654C' : col}"/>`;
    return g;
  }
  function draw() {
    let g = panel(26, 110, 19.78, 20.32, xs, MU, () => MU + 3 * SX, () => MU - 3 * SX, sigX, '#0F6E6B', 'X-bar chart, limits 19.82 to 20.28');
    g += panel(176, 100, 19.98, 20.13, ew, MU, (i) => MU + lim[i], (i) => MU - lim[i], sigE, '#E29A2D', 'EWMA chart, λ = 0.1');
    if (shown === N) { const X = (i) => 70 + i / (N - 1) * (1160 - 90); g += `<line x1="${X(15) - 10}" x2="${X(15) - 10}" y1="20" y2="285" stroke="#1C242B" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="3 3"/><text x="${X(15) - 4}" y="296" font-size="14" fill="#1C242B">drift starts</text>`; }
    document.getElementById('ddx-svg').innerHTML = g;
    document.getElementById('ddx-n').textContent = `Subgroup ${shown} of ${N}`;
    const msg = [];
    if (sigX >= 0 && shown > sigX) msg.push(`X-bar signals at subgroup ${sigX + 1}`);
    if (sigE >= 0 && shown > sigE) msg.push(`<span class="best">EWMA signals at subgroup ${sigE + 1}</span>`);
    document.getElementById('ddx-out').innerHTML = msg.length ? msg.join('; ') + '.' : (shown ? 'No signal yet. Would you stop the line?' : 'Press "Next subgroup" to reveal the first hour.');
    if (shown === N) document.getElementById('ddx-out').innerHTML += ` A drift of +1 σ<sub>x̄</sub> (0.077 mg/cm²) was planted from subgroup 16.${sigX < 0 ? ' The X-bar chart never signals.' : ''}`;
  }
  document.getElementById('ddx-next').addEventListener('click', () => { if (shown < N) shown++; draw(); });
  document.getElementById('ddx-all').addEventListener('click', () => { shown = N; draw(); });
  document.getElementById('ddx-rst').addEventListener('click', () => { shown = 0; draw(); });
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

## Activity · Drift detectives {#act1 .activity data-hold="true"}

[Groups of 4 · 25 minutes · detection time for each chart]{.act-label}

::: {.prompt}
Subgroup means are revealed one hour at a time. Update both charts on paper. Raise the red card at your first signal on either chart.
:::

1. Before you start: compute the X-bar limits and the EWMA limits for the first three subgroups.
2. Plot each new mean on the X-bar chart and update z~t~ on the EWMA chart.
3. Record the subgroup at which each chart first signals, and whether you would have stopped the line earlier on judgment alone.
4. At the end, the drift point is revealed. How many hours of drifted coating did each chart let through?

## Activity · Answer {#act1-answer}

::: {.two}
::: {}
```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Chart</th><th class="num">First signal</th><th class="num">Hours after drift began</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>X-bar, 3σ only</td><td class="num">none in 30</td><td class="num">more than 14</td></tr>
    <tr><td>X-bar with run rules</td><td class="num">26</td><td class="num">10</td></tr>
    <tr><td>CUSUM</td><td class="num">23</td><td class="num">7</td></tr>
    <tr><td>EWMA</td><td class="num hit">22</td><td class="num">6</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```
The drift of +0.077 mg/cm² started at subgroup 16.
:::
::: {}
Six hours of slightly heavy coating is still well inside the specification: the coupons stay near 20.13, far from 20.6. That is the point of SPC: act on the process before the product goes out of specification.

One dataset is one draw. The run-length table says what to expect on average.
:::
:::

## What we learned {#debrief}

::: {.takeaways}
::: {.tk}
Rational subgroups put short-term noise inside the subgroup, so changes over time show between subgroups.
:::
::: {.tk}
Read the R chart before the X-bar chart. Control limits describe the process; specifications describe the customer's need.
:::
::: {.tk .key}
For small sustained drifts, EWMA and CUSUM signal several times faster than an X-bar chart at the same false-alarm rate.
:::
:::
